answer: Each new agent starts with no earning rights and must pass one slow identity check on a single verification thread. The check binds the agent to one quartz-timed hardware clock, so one machine cannot pose as many agents. Rights then grow only as verified work crosses a rising ridge: 10 tasks in 30 days, then 50, then 200. A fake identity costs a fresh clock plus the full 30 day wait, and a fake caught reusing another clock record loses every right at once.
